clue.text: Deal with proposal

blocks.note: first meaning: a verb, to tackle a problem or task
second meaning: a noun, an overture or suggestion put to someone

explanation.walkthrough: The oblique stroke marks where one meaning stops and the other starts; the first is a verb and the second a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: You tackle a problem by finding a way in, and an overture or offer made to someone is also called by this word.

clue.text: Most famous listed building here?

blocks.note: surface reading: a town known for its grade-listed heritage architecture
setter's reading: listed means tilted or leaning, as a ship lists, so this is the home of the best-known leaning tower

explanation.surface: A heritage question: which place has the most celebrated protected building?
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a listed building is one protected for its history, but a ship that lists leans over; the famous leaning tower is in this Italian city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian city is home to the campanile famous for tilting, the most celebrated leaning building anywhere in the world.

clue.text: Arterial route in China or Taiwan

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words that follows, so the answer is found within them

blocks.note: spanning the end of the first word, the whole middle word and the start of the last

explanation.surface: A trunk road or main highway running through China or Taiwan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arterial route' reads like a main road on a map, but the route is in the body: the main artery leaving the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the body's largest artery, the main channel carrying blood from the heart, so it is literally an arterial route.

clue.text: Silver used in renovated Christian emblem

indicators.note: something renovated has been done up and rebuilt, so the letters are rearranged into a new form

blocks.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Silver has been worked into a restored religious symbol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Used in' looks like it tells you where the silver goes, but both words are simply letters to rearrange after AG.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lamb of God, a lamb carrying a cross or banner, is a traditional symbol of Christ in church art and heraldry.

clue.text: Rough diamonds in Parisian street

indicators.note: one thing placed in another ends up enclosed by it

blocks.note: D is the card-game abbreviation for the diamonds suit
rue is French for street

explanation.surface: Uncut gems turning up on a street in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough diamonds' reads as one phrase, uncut stones; split it, and the first word is the definition while diamonds gives only a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something crude, primitive or roughly made is described with this adjective, as in a basic shelter or a coarse remark.

clue.text: Does it store all the letters one writes?

definitions.text: Does it store all the letters one writes?

blocks.clueFragment: Does it store all the letters one writes?
blocks.note: surface reading: a filing cabinet or archive keeping every piece of correspondence someone sends
setter's reading: the letters are characters of writing, and the full set of them is what every written word is drawn from

explanation.surface: Wondering where someone keeps copies of all the letters they write.
explanation.walkthrough: Letters suggests correspondence and store suggests a file; think instead of the characters themselves, the complete set from A to Z.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the complete ordered set of characters used in writing a language, the stock every written word draws from.

clue.text: Hot wind causes shock

blocks.note: H is the usual abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
a light wind or breeze is moving air

explanation.surface: A scorching wind gives people a nasty fright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' looks like a fright, but here it is a thick mass, as in a shock of red hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A shock is a thick, bushy, untidy mass, and the phrase is almost always used of what grows on someone's head.

clue.text: Branch installing new vault

indicators.note: to install something is to fit it inside, so one piece takes another within it

blocks.note: a sprig is a small shoot or twig
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A bank branch having a new strongroom fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: Branch and vault conjure a bank with its strongroom; in fact the branch is a twig and the vault is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: To vault is to leap or jump over something, and that is exactly what it means to spring over a fence.

clue.text: Metal to conduct

blocks.note: first meaning: the heavy grey metallic element, rhyming with bed
second meaning: to guide or direct, rhyming with bead

explanation.walkthrough: The two meanings are spelt the same but pronounced differently, which helps hide the second.
explanation.definitionFit: The heavy soft element Pb shares its spelling with the verb meaning to guide, direct or be in charge of.

clue.text: Cute and rare wild animal

indicators.note: something wild is unruly and out of control, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An endearing, uncommon wild animal, the sort a nature documentary features.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild animal' reads as a single phrase, but wild is the anagram signal and only animal is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Any living beast can be called by this general word for an animal, especially a small or endearing one.

clue.text: Wounded Romeo put inside cabin

indicators.note: what is put inside something ends up enclosed by it

blocks.note: a hut is a small simple cabin
Romeo is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for R

explanation.surface: An injured Romeo is carried into a cabin to recover.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo is not Shakespeare's lover here but the radio code word for the letter R.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone injured or harmed is described by this past participle, as in badly injured in the accident.

clue.text: Handed over dollar and avoided duty

blocks.note: first meaning, taken literally: a buck is slang for a dollar, and passing it is handing it on
second meaning: the idiom for shifting responsibility onto someone else

explanation.surface: Someone gave away a dollar and then shirked their responsibilities.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads the idiom literally; the second half gives its everyday meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means shifting responsibility or blame to someone else, dodging an obligation that should have been yours.

clue.text: Lost son alive in the country

indicators.note: something lost has gone astray, so the letters wander out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A missing son is found living somewhere abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Son' would usually give S, but here the whole word is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a small nation in central Europe bordering Italy, Austria, Hungary and Croatia, with Ljubljana as its capital.

clue.text: Mum boards tall ship for solemn celebration

indicators.note: a passenger who boards gets on and is then inside the vessel

blocks.note: tall and high both mean of great height
SS is short for steamship
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Mother goes aboard a tall ship for an important ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tall ship' reads as a sailing vessel, but it splits into HIGH and the steamship abbreviation SS, and mum climbs aboard between the two.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the full Catholic service with music, incense and ceremony, sung rather than said, and so especially solemn.

clue.text: Two coppers, married, live on river — it’s cool!

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, taken twice
M is the standard abbreviation for married
to be is to exist or live
R is the usual abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Two police officers marry and settle on a houseboat, and it is all very relaxed.
explanation.walkthrough: Coppers look like police but are the element copper; the definition leans on the saying cool as a cucumber.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying cool as a cucumber makes this salad vegetable the proverbial example of something calm and chilled.

clue.text: Scottish king worried about old country seat?

indicators.note: something worried has been shaken and tugged about, so the letters are jumbled
about means around, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A fretful Scottish monarch fussing over an old stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: A country seat sounds like a stately home; the question mark hints it is literally something to sit on in the country.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a spiked walking stick whose handle unfolds into a small seat, used by spectators at field sports and race meetings.

clue.text: Character from SW?

blocks.note: first meaning: the general quality or feel of something
second meaning: a river of Somerset in south-west England, which flows through Taunton

explanation.walkthrough: SW is the compass abbreviation for south-west; the question mark flags that the second meaning is a place-name, the Somerset river, rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: The general quality, mood or feel of a place or piece of writing is its character, and also what this word names.

clue.text: Sign from ladies losing weight

indicators.note: whatever is lost is no longer there, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: ladies are women
W is the standard abbreviation for weight

explanation.surface: Proof from women who have been dieting that it is working.
explanation.walkthrough: Losing weight suggests a diet; it means dropping the letter that stands for weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A portent or augury of what is to come is a sign of the future, good or bad.

clue.text: Former tie broken in WW1 battlefield

indicators.note: something broken is smashed apart, so its letters can be rearranged
one thing placed in another ends up enclosed by it

blocks.note: the three letters rearranged
the Somme in northern France saw one of the bloodiest battles of the First World War

explanation.surface: An old bond of friendship shattered on the Western Front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Former tie' reads as an old link or relationship, but former is the definition standing alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, as in the sometime mayor, it means one-time or previous, the same as former.

clue.text: Potato small and sweet

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small
pud is informal British for pudding, a dessert

explanation.surface: A little sweet potato described on a menu.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a sweet is a dessert, and pud, short for pudding, is the everyday word for one.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an informal, affectionate slang word for a potato, heard across Britain, Ireland and Australia.

clue.text: What’s changed in warmer weather?

indicators.note: something that is changed is altered in form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking what is different about the world when the weather warms up.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a question, but its first word is the letters to rearrange and the rest defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A spell of milder conditions when ice and snow start melting is named by this noun, so it is warmer weather.

clue.text: So far, one mythical hairy creature

blocks.note: as yet means up to now, so far
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Up to now only one legendary shaggy beast has been recorded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So far' is a two-word phrase that gives one short word, as yet; the definition is the whole of the rest after 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: The abominable snowman of Himalayan legend is a shaggy ape-like beast whose existence has never been proven.

clue.text: Some girls have nails closely cut

indicators.note: only a portion of the following words is wanted, a run of their letters

blocks.note: the last letter of the first word, the whole second word and the first letter of the third

explanation.surface: A remark that some girls keep their fingernails trimmed short.
explanation.walkthrough: Nails closely cut seems to be the definition, but only the final two words define, describing hair taken right down.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair removed right down to the skin with a razor is the result of a very close cut, as on a clean chin.

clue.text: Edna turned south for the mountains

indicators.note: something turned is faced the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the compass abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Edna changed direction and headed south toward the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned south' reads as a single change of direction, but turned acts on the name alone and south simply follows.
explanation.definitionFit: This long mountain chain runs down the western edge of South America, the longest continental range on Earth.
